ordinary_frame.basis: This remains a Mass. The normal formulary appoints Oratio super populum after Postcommunion and before dismissal (Missale Romanum 1962, printed p. 117, numbered text 752; artifact PDF p. 198). The held generic Ordinary frame has no declared place for this prayer, so that frame is unavailable. The Propers remain in their printed order.

The 1962 reading was established on that edition's page images rather than its text layer, cross-read against the Benziger conformed printing. Differences from the antecedent: 1862 text layer damages 6 place(s) in this prayer; at each the 1962 word and the layer's reading are: fiat -> flat; nostre -> nostrse; tune -> tunc; proderunt suscepta -> pr derunt susc pta; tue -> tuai; placita -> pldcita; 1922 Mame text layer damages 4 place(s) here (chiefly its OCR of the ae/oe ligatures and of the acute accents): fiat -> iat; (nothing) -> f; fructuosus -> fructudsus; deuotionis -> deuotidnis; both antecedents print the ae and oe ligatures and the printed acute accents, and use the j-orthography; this transcription follows the repository convention recorded in src/sources/calendars/roman-1962/propers.yaml (j retained, ae/oe digraphs written as two letters, no accent marks). Corroboration: 1922 Mame, editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (public domain), printed p. 148, artifact PDF p. 262; Benziger 1962 conformed printing OCR at djvu text line 33223 (comparison witness only, rights_status unresolved; never a publication basis); the 1604 and 1570 were not consulted for this oration - the 1862 and the 1922 Mame between them read the whole prayer.

propers.text:

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.
